32472-food-in-war-time.creator: W. B. Saunders Company
32472-food-in-war-time.description: A book by W. B. Saunders Company. Italian peasants of southern Italy. Two Italian scientists describe how this class of people live mainly on cornmeal, olive oil, and green stuffs and have done so for generations. There is no milk, cheese, or eggs in their dietary.

arxiv-2101-03658.title: Approximation and quadrature by weighted least squares polynomials on the sphere
arxiv-2101-03658.creator: Wanting Lu, Heping Wang
arxiv-2101-03658.description: Abstract . Given a sequence of Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities in L 2 L_{2} on a usual compact space ℳ \mathcal{M} , Gröchenig in [ 11 ] introduced the weighted least squares polynomials and the least squares quadrature from pointwise samples of a function, and obtained approximation theorems and quadrature errors.

arxiv-2212-01880.title: Deep Learning for Multiscale Damage Analysis via Physics-Informed Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2212-01880.creator: Shiguang Deng, Shirin Hosseinmardi, Diran Apelian, Ramin Bostanabad
arxiv-2212-01880.description: Abstract Abstract Direct numerical simulation of hierarchical materials via homogenization-based concurrent multiscale models poses critical challenges for 3D large scale engineering applications, as the computation of highly nonlinear and path-dependent material constitutive responses at the fine scale causes prohibitively high computational costs.

arxiv-2405-19681.title: Bayesian Online Natural Gradient ( bong )
arxiv-2405-19681.creator: Matt Jones, Peter Chang, Kevin Murphy
arxiv-2405-19681.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Matt Jones, Peter Chang, Kevin Murphy. We propose a novel approach to sequential Bayesian inference based on variational Bayes (VB). The key insight is that, in the online setting, we do not need to add the KL term to regularize to the prior (which comes from the posterior at the previous timestep); instead we can optimize just the expected log-likelihood, performing a single step of natural gradient descent starting at the prior predictive.

Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the Europea
arxiv-2405-20263.creator: Roman Feller, Michael Pinsker
arxiv-2405-20263.description: Abstract . For a set ℱ \mathcal{F} of finite tournaments, the ℱ \mathcal{F} -free orientation problem is the problem of orienting a given finite undirected graph in such a way that the resulting oriented graph does not contain any member of ℱ \mathcal{F} .

arxiv-2502-20478.title: Explainable AI for Clinical Outcome Prediction: A Survey of Clinician Perceptions and Preferences
arxiv-2502-20478.creator: Jun Hou, MS 1, Lucy Lu Wang, PhD 2
arxiv-2502-20478.description: Abstract Explainable AI (XAI) techniques are necessary to help clinicians make sense of AI predictions and integrate predictions into their decision-making workflow. In this work, we conduct a survey study to understand clinician preference among different XAI techniques when they are used to interpret model predictions over text-based EHR data.

arxiv-2506-14046.title: Ace-CEFR - A Dataset for Automated Evaluation of the Linguistic Difficulty of Conversational Texts for LLM Applications
arxiv-2506-14046.creator: David Kogan, Max Schumacher, Sam Nguyen
arxiv-2506-14046.description: Abstract There is an unmet need to evaluate the language difficulty of short, conversational passages of text, particularly for training and filtering Large Language Models (LLMs). We introduce Ace-CEFR, a dataset of English conversational text passages expert-annotated with their corresponding level of text difficulty. We experiment with several models on Ace-CEFR, including Transformer-based models and LLMs.

pmc-10668088.title: Does the choice of chemoprophylaxis affect the prevention of deep vein thrombosis in lumbar fusion surgery? A systematic review of the literature☆
pmc-10668088.creator: Sathish Muthu, Georgios Mavrovounis, Stipe Corluka, Zorica Buser, Giovanni Barbanti Brodano, Yabin Wu, Hans-Jorg Meisel, Jeffrey Wang, S Tim Yoon, Andreas K Demetriades, AO Spine Knowledge Forum Degenerative
pmc-10668088.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionTo date, the available guidance on venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in elective lumbar fusion surgery is largely open to surgeon interpretation and preference without any specific suggested chemoprophylactic regimen.Research questionThis study aimed to comparatively analyze the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) with the use of commonly employed chemoprophylactic agents such as unfractionated heparin (UH) and low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) in lumbar fusion surgery.Material and methodsAn independent systematic review of four scientific databases (PubMed, Scopus, clinicaltrials.gov, Web

pmc-11388080.title: EBV-associated epithelial cancers cells promote vasculogenic mimicry formation via a secretory cross-talk with the immune microenvironment
pmc-11388080.creator: Tong Xiang, Fengze Sun, Tingting Liu, Jingjing Zhao, Jieying Yang, Dijun Ouyang, Hao Chen, Qian Zhu, Qijing Wang, Yongqiang Li, Jia He, Chaopin Yang, Xinyi Yang, Yuanyuan Chen, Yan Tang, Desheng Weng, Qiuzhong Pan, Qi Yang, Jianchuan Xia
pmc-11388080.description: Background: Vasculogenic mimicry (VM) induced by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection plays an important role in resistance to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy in EBV-associated epithelial cancers; however, the interaction between VM and the immune microenvironment has not been systematically investigated.

pmc-11473807.title: A post-Brexit intergroup contact intervention reduces affective polarization between Leavers and Remainers short-term
pmc-11473807.creator: Nicole Tausch, Michèle D. Birtel, Paulina Górska, Sidney Bode, Carolina Rocha
pmc-11473807.description: With mounting evidence of the harmful societal consequences of affective polarization, it is crucial to find ways of addressing it. Employing a randomized controlled trial, this study tested the effectiveness of an intervention based on theories of intergroup contact and interpersonal communication in reducing affective polarization in the context of Brexit. Participants were 120 UK self-identified Leavers and Remainers.

pmc-11585768.title: PKC-mediated phosphorylation governs the stability and function of CELF1 as a driver of EMT in breast epithelial cells
pmc-11585768.creator: Shebna Massey, Natee Kongchan, Yang Gao, Arindam Chaudhury, Emuejevoke Olokpa, Jason Karch, Anna Malovannaya, Chonghui Cheng, Xiang Zhang, Joel R. Neilson
pmc-11585768.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) is believed to be a principal factor contributing to cancer metastasis. The post-transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms underlying EMT are comparatively underexplored. We previously demonstrated that the CELF1 RNA binding protein is necessary and sufficient to drive the EMT of breast epithelial cells, and that the relative protein expression of CELF1 in this context was dictated at the post-translational level. Here, we elucidate the mechanism of this regulation.

pmc-11603428.title: Dissecting Causal Links Between Gut Microbiota, Inflammatory Cytokines, and Parkinson's Disease: A Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11603428.creator: Ma Caiyun, Wen Hebao, Ye Wenhao, Liu Changqing, Li Changqing, Zhao Xiaojiang
pmc-11603428.description: BackgroundThe association between gut microbiota (GM) and Parkinson's disease (PD) has been well established, but whether there is a causal relationship between the two and whether inflammatory cytokines (ICs) act as mediators remain unclear.Methods:We utilized the summary databases of large‐scale genome‐wide association studies (GWAS) conducting Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses to investigate the causal relationships between GM, ICs, and PD.

pmc-11608201.title: Evaluating KLHDC8A as a biomarker for glioma: impact on survival and proliferation through the Wnt/β-catenin pathway
pmc-11608201.creator: Yu Tian, Xiaofei Hu, Xiaoling Wang, Youcai Huang, Junfeng Hao, Yu Guo, Chao Zhu, Yanyang Tu
pmc-11608201.description: Glioma is one of the most common malignant tumors and shows a high metastasis rate and poor prognosis. KLHDC8A has been implicated in several cancers, but its role in glioma and its potential as a biomarker remain unclear. We conducted a pan-cancer analysis of KLHDC8A using multiple databases and assessed its expression levels, survival associations, and diagnostic utility.

pmc-12632225.title: Dissociation in focus: replicating and extending network analytic insights based on the dissociative experiences scale
pmc-12632225.creator: Philipp Wülfing, Carsten Spitzer, Judy Leibowitz, Stephen Pilling, Peter Fonagy, London Personality and Mood Disorder Consortium, Read Montague, Tobias Nolte
pmc-12632225.description: Background: Factor-analytic studies of the Dissociative Experiences Scale (DES) have reported between one- and seven-factor solutions, leaving its dimensional architecture unresolved. This inconsistency compromises the interpretability of scores and limits the scale’s utility for screening and treatment planning. To ensure diagnostic relevance and capture dissociation across mental disorders, we focused on a clinical cohort.

pmc-12732451.title: Functional Coupling of Calcium-Sensing Receptor and Polycystin-2 in Renal Epithelial Cells: Physiological Role and Potential Therapeutic Target in Polycystic Kidney Disease
pmc-12732451.creator: Annarita Di Mise, Angela Ferrulli, Mariangela Centrone, Maria Venneri, Marianna Ranieri, Grazia Tamma, Rosa Caroppo, Giovanna Valenti
pmc-12732451.description: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is caused by mutations in PKD1 or PKD2 genes, encoding polycystin-1 (PC1) or polycystin-2 (PC2), respectively, characterized by excessive cell proliferation and fluid secretion, resulting in renal cyst formation and growth. PC1 and PC2 form a complex localized on the plasma membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and primary cilia.

pmc-13194214.title: Traumatic intraventricular haemorrhages: clinical indicators determining morbidity and mortality in paediatric patients
pmc-13194214.creator: Zeynep Ölmez Mart, Emel Ulusoy, Bahar Uyuşkan, İlknur Akansu, Anıl Er, Koray Ur, Öznur Eser, Merve Eraslan Canbeldek, Özge Günal, Murat Duman
pmc-13194214.description: Intracranial haemorrhages and traumatic brain injury are significant causes of morbidity and mortality in paediatric patients. Traumatic intraventricular haemorrhage (tIVH) is the least common type of intracranial haemorrhage and typically occurs in association with other intracranial injuries. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics of children diagnosed with tIVH, and to identify risk factors associated with poor prognosis.

pmc-13199572.title: Neointimal hyperplasia and vascular restenosis: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic interventions
pmc-13199572.creator: Lingyan Yi, Tingting Chen, Yulin Zhou, Peile Zhu, Qingyu Zhu, Yuting Shao, Wenjuan Yao
pmc-13199572.description: Vascular restenosis, a pathological recurrence of lumen narrowing following interventions, remains a major limitation to the long-term success of vascular procedures. Its development is centrally driven by neointimal hyperplasia, a process orchestrated by endothelial injury, phenotypic switching of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) from a contractile to a synthetic state, and a coordinated inflammatory response.

pmc-13391541.title: Recent advances in superwetting anti-fog surfaces for medical goggles: a mini review
pmc-13391541.creator: Qiuxu Guo, Jing Hu, Yongfeng Wang, Lei Wang
pmc-13391541.description: Medical goggles often suffer from fogging and droplet adhesion in high-humidity or long-term use, severely impairing visual clarity. Superwetting anti-fog surfaces have gained attention, primarily focusing on superhydrophilic and superhydrophobic surfaces. This mini review systematically discusses the mechanism and performance of these approaches, with particular emphasis on their applications in medical goggles.

pmc-13626917.title: Dimethyl malonate suppresses succinate dehydrogenase to alleviate ischemia/reperfusion-induced acute lung injury
pmc-13626917.creator: Shih-En Tang, Shu-Yu Wu, Hsin-Ping Pao, Shi-Jye Chu, Wen-I Liao
pmc-13626917.description: BackgroundIschemia/reperfusion (IR) injury is a pivotal contributor to acute lung injury (ALI) for which effective treatment options are currently lacking. Following ischemia, succinate accumulation and reoxidation by succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) during reperfusion induce excessive reactive oxygen species production, causing significant tissue damage.
